{"design":"PLAN (draft 2026-11-02, awaiting Mark's approval). Haven checkout: ~/GIT/haven-interop @ 2c14e62 (Apache-2.0 LICENSE file present; GitHub API reports no license).

Constraints from Haven's DIVERGENCES.md: mimi-hubd never calls another provider (DIV-5), has no groupInfo (DIV-1), and processes only update Commits carrying exactly one custom proposal (DIV-10). So live traffic is one-way: mimid -> mimi-hubd TLS-PL lane (/mimi/pl/*): keyMaterial, submitMessage, requestConsent/updateConsent, identifierQuery, reportAbuse, update(single custom proposal). mimi-hubd requires mTLS (fails closed).

Phase A, offline wire cross-check (first; no network; fits AGENTS.md fixture rules):
A1. A small generator crate committed under crates/mimi-protocol/tests/fixtures/haven/gen/ (NOT a workspace member, no mimid dependency on Haven) builds Haven mimi-core at a pinned commit and writes TLS-PL bytes for every request/response it encodes. mimid's mimi-protocol decodes each one, compares with the expected value, re-encodes, and requires identical bytes. PROVENANCE: repo, commit, SHA-256, license.
A2. Reverse direction: mimid-encoded fixtures decoded by Haven's decoders, run locally in the Haven checkout. No write to their repo; results go to findings.
Every mismatch becomes a bead: mimid bug, Haven divergence (report on havenmessenger/interop with Mark's per-action OK), or a spec ambiguity (decision bead + wg bead).

Phase B, live (after A):
B1. Directory: mimid requires all 10 keys (mimi-protocol/src/directory.rs:122-138); Haven lists only the endpoints it implements, so mimid cannot parse it. Needs a decision bead on protocol-06 section 5.1 (is a partial directory valid?).
B2. Haven's submitMessage template is {recipient}, not protocol-06's {roomId}: a Haven divergence to report.
B3. mTLS: mimid's PeerClient has no client certificate (peer.rs:124-129), deliberately (no provider authentication). Proposed: the harness puts a local TLS proxy holding the client certificate between mimid and mimi-hubd; mimid code unchanged.
B4. Harness: a script plus an ignored-by-default test (or a manual runbook) that starts mimi-hubd with throwaway certificates and drives mimid's PeerClient against it. Not in CI (tests must be offline).

Known likely mismatch: Haven resolves ParticipantListUpdate indices against alphabetical URI order (DIV-10 caveat), and mimid uses list order (decision .5.70)."}
